The '''[[1889 in association football|1889]]–[[1890 in association football|90]] Football League''' was the second season of English league [[Association football|football]], with [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] being crowned as the champions for the second successive season. The clubs competing were the 12 original clubs which were the founders of the league the previous year. Unlike the modern system, two points were awarded for a win, with one for a draw and no points for a loss; this system remained until three points for a win were awarded beginning with the [[1981–82 Football League|1981–82]] season.

==Final league table==
During the first five seasons of the league (until the [[1893–94 Football League|1893–94]] season), the re-election process concerned the clubs which finished in the bottom four of the league.<ref name="Rothmans">Ian Laschke: ''Rothmans Book of Football League Records 1888–89 to 1978–79''. Macdonald and Jane’s, London & Sydney, 1980.</ref>

==Re-election process==
At the Football League election meeting no vote was taken, and it was agreed that [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]] were re-elected and that [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] was elected in place of [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke]], who played in the [[1890–91 Football Alliance|Football Alliance]] the following season but returned to the Football League after a year's absence.

The applications of [[Football Alliance]] sides [[Bootle F.C. (1879)|Bootle]], [[Darwen F.C. (1870)|Darwen]], [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Newton Heath]] and [[Sunderland Albion F.C.|Sunderland Albion]] were rejected.<ref>[http://www.footballsite.co.uk/Statistics/NonLeagueTables/FA1889-90.htm footballsite.co.uk]</ref>
